body_text: The truth is out there! Maybe. The pollster Gallup has been asking people if they’ve seen a UFO for over fifty years, and the fraction is now higher than ever, with 17% of people saying they’ve seen something they thought was a UFO , up from 9% in 1978. Certainly that has nothing to do with the rise of the personal UAV market, a parabolic increase in satellites, the commercial space launch industry, the Starlink constellation, drone shows, more weather balloons, increased commercial flight frequencies, the more frequent documentation of otherwise standard atmospheric optical phenomena, digital artifacts inherent in phone cameras, the legalization of marijuana, the rising acceptability of hallucinogens, people being under a lot of stress these days, increased light pollution, or commercial UAV use. Surely it’s the aliens. Stocks were down on Friday after the Chairman of the Federal Reserve indicated he might be worried about inflation (more on that below!) but finished the week up. Last week we heard from the man who runs the most important central bank in America. Later in the week, we also heard from the Fed Chair. Yes, Nvidia earnings coupled with the Fed’s annual symposium at Jackson Hole meant that we got an unusually high degree of candor from the two institutions upon which today’s markets rely most heavily. First, the Fed. Chairman Kevin Warsh spoke at Jackson Hole and, with the rhetorical strategic ambiguity that defines the institution, affirmed that the 2% inflation target is absolutely an important priority and — while he didn’t say when rates would go up or by how much they would rise — the market took his point. The market-implied chance of a rate hike in 2026 increased from 59% to 69% * as traders read between the lines. Second, Nvidia. Nvidia has been described as the central bank of AI by Luke Kawa, the writer behind the now must-read Entrypoint newsletter , and that could not be more apt now. The chip juggernaut realized early on in the AI boom that it could — and arguably must — leverage its vast resources, investing in its customers and suppliers and even prospective rivals in order to play this technology out to its fullest. Nvidia’s public and private equity holdings reached $95.6 billion at the end of July, including stakes in Intel , CoreWeave , and Nebius. By comparison, that figure was under $100 million as recently as 2020. It’s also guaranteeing a whole lot of investment, with the company disclosing $108.5 billion in guarantees, most of which is tied to OpenAI’s data center buildout . While the details are still a bit murky, reports last week that Nvidia was making a move on Hugging Face , the repository of models that has been the central clearinghouse of decentralized models for much of the boom; this would give Nvidia a solid strategic position as OpenAI seeks to create its own chips. Earlier this month, Nvidia and a consortium of Wall Street groups announced $500 billion in capital to provide financing for customers to pay for compute. But is Nvidia getting too far out ahead of its skis, doling out too much money elsewhere while its own shareholders get nothing? Heck no, its projected revenue will increase 70% next year, well above the 45% expectation, and the market responded by making its stock go up one Palantir. “What is Nvidia” should be a rather simple question — they make chips, chips that have become very important for the economy, and they have made strategic investments to both expand and protect that business — but for traders, Nvidia is especially interesting because for a manufacturer of semiconductors it sure doesn’t trade like a semiconductor manufacturer. From Kawa’s EntryPoint : “Nvidia is barely behaving like a semiconductor company. The most valuable publicly traded company has a correlation of near zero with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index!” Instead, he writes, “The company is no longer a hardware seller whose high-powered offerings are well-supported by a software that developers are intimately familiar and comfortable with [...] the stock has become more of an amorphous bet on the future of AI, because it’s taken on a role as a facilitator of the growth of the entire ecosystem.” Nvidia is living the poker player’s dream: make enough good plays with the chips, soon you’re running the table, and eventually you just become The House. *Event contracts are offered through Robinhood Derivatives, LLC — probabilities referenced or sourced from KalshiEx LLC or ForecastEx LLC. 🎬 Oscars: We are a week away from TIFF, the film festival where many serious Oscar contenders will make their debut. One to watch out for is, incidentally, “The Debut,” which is directed by Jesse Eisenberg and stars Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti. Moore is currently an early favorite for Best Actress, with markets pricing a 31% chance . 🎮 Five Star Wanted Level: Thursday’s exclusive look into GTA6 has certainly increased expectations around the game, with market prices indicating a 75% chance it wins the Game of the Year award for 2026 as of Friday, up from 59% earlier in the week. Texas’ power grid, after a rough couple of years, is having an incredibly boring summer , and it’s thanks to a build out of batteries that has allowed the grid to use its vast solar energy generation ability as the sun begins to set. On August 23, ERCOT set a record for maximum battery discharge: 13,256 megawatts at 7:45 pm . This feels decisively bearish on putting datacenters in orbit , which is after all lousy with cosmic rays. title: ⛈️ Any airport in a storm
body_text: A 23-year-old Polish man may soon be served a sizable slice of justice after allegedly placing a run of prank pizza orders to homes of politicians and local media figures, one of which was for some 300 pizzas worth more than 37,000 Polish Zloty… or ~$10,000. Although tedious fake calls and fraudulent pay-on-delivery orders aren’t exactly uncommon at pizza places or other delivery restaurants, the details of this case go further than your average pie-shop prank. The accused reportedly used personal details of his intended recipients and made threats of violence and references to other criminal activity when placing orders — all of which combined to see him face up to eight years in prison on charges of identity fraud, stalking, and causing significant financial harm to the businesses he targeted. The S&P 500 rose 0.7% and the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.4% Thursday, as Nvidia posted the second-largest single-day market cap gain ever in the wake of its strong Q2 earnings and robust guidance. There are fewer more jarring moments in the modern travel experience than making it through the security process and battling thronging crowds of people who seem to have never been in an airport (or possibly even outside the house) before, only to be greeted by your fate writ large in glowing LED lettering on the departure board as you see the vague and dreaded “DELAYED” notice next to your flight number. Sadly the issue, like those who fall victim to it, is going nowhere fast. According to figures from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, 21.58% of flights across America’s 10 largest carriers have been delayed so far this year; if that trend holds for the rest of 2026, it’ll be the fifth year in a row where more than one in five flights has been held up. If that stat hasn’t left those of you with big travel plans for the Labor Day weekend anxious enough, the flight cancellation rate is also currently 2.2%, the highest it's been since 2022. A separate set of numbers from the Bureau reported by Business Insider earlier this week revealed that some of the biggest airports in the US are often where fliers can expect to run into the most timing trouble. In the six months from January to June, the ten airports with the lowest on-time departure rates saw 29.8% of all flights delayed on average, with Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood airport, where 33.6% of scheduled flights don’t leave on time, landing as the worst of the bunch. That’s obviously not great for anyone who’s used the Florida airport so far this year, but with just ~114,000 scheduled flights and 15.6 million enplaned passengers in 2025, delay rates at other airports on the list will have affected much larger swaths of the population. Dallas-Fort Worth, for instance, boarded 41.3 million passengers in 2025 meaning that if the 31.8% delay rate held up for the whole year, fliers were spread evenly across affected flights, and the passenger level stayed roughly the same, over 13 million passengers can expect a longer wait at the Texas airport than anticipated in 2026. Even in a year when Spirit Airlines, a carrier notoriously haggard by hold-ups through the years , folded operations and sold off its highly-sought slots at LaGuardia — the ninth most-delayed airport in the US, interestingly — it feels like anyone looking for a quick fix for the American air travel industry’s great delay issue might have to wait a little longer yet. That’s roughly how many more hours Harry Styles will spend on the Madison Square Garden stage over the remaining 29 legs of his 30-date run, having kicked off his residency on Wednesday with a career-spanning show that clocked in at around 1 hour 50 minutes. 11.5 million people signed up for presale ticket access, a record for a single artist in the New York market, per Ticketmaster , though many Styles fans felt affronted when the Garden tickets were released, with top VIP seats costing as much as $1,667. HP Inc reported that unit shipments of personal systems (laptops, computers, notebooks etc) dropped 16% in Q3 from the same period last year, though segment revenue still rose 18% on price hikes. In the wake of Nvidia’s better-than-expected earnings results and whopping FY2028 sales forecast, it’s now reported that the company is also closing in on acquiring open-source platform Hugging Face, which allows users to share machine learning models and datasets, for almost $13 billion. Dolly Parton streams rocketed on Spotify in the days following the country legend and philanthropist’s passing — US streams were up 2,320% from the daily average on Wednesday , as “Jolene” and “9 to 5” rose to number 2 and 3 on Spotify’s US chart. Just 12% of American adults say they make “all or almost all” of their purchases in cash across an average week, compared to 24% who said the same in 2015, according to a new survey from Pew Research Center. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is set to make his debut speech at Jackson Hole at 10 a.m. ET today.

title: 🤯 Nvidia's bombshell earnings call
body_text: All great consumer freakouts happen twice: the first time as farce, and the second time, well, they’re still a farce Surging prices, dwindling supply, and hoarding of a household basic. The Covid-induced Great Toiler Paper Freak Out of 2020 – far from one of the more significant hardships of the pandemic – could possibly return as a trade-war induced variant. A large amount of US toilet paper is made in America, but a huge amount of the raw paper pulp used to manufacture it comes from Canada. And in the spiralling US-Canada trade war, Canada is now set to put a 2-50% tariff on US-made toilet paper and facial tissue in response to US tariff hikes on imported Canadian paper goods. US retailers like Costco are likely to be hit with higher costs: the bulk-goods purveyor sources the majority of its paper products from Canada, the Guardian reports . Procter & Gamble, which owns Charmin, said last year it was raising prices in part due to tariffs. Stocks dipped ever so slightly on Wednesday. Nvidia releases better-than-expected quarterly earnings and the stock falls afterwards. If that sounds a bit familiar, there’s a good reason: going into Wednesday’s aftermarket earnings release, that is precisely what has happened for each of the last four quarters, as Sherwood News’ Luke Kawa wrote in the Entrypoint newsletter . At first, nothing much seemed to have changed: Nvidia reported earnings per share of $2.22 and revenue of $96.22 billion after the market closed yesterday afternoon, ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of $2.10 in earnings per share and $92.17 billion in revenue. In response, the stock dipped. But then, Nvidia’s chief financial officer Collette Kress dropped a bombshell. On the company’s post-earnings conference calls, she said executives expected the company’s fiscal-year 2028 revenue to rise by a staggering 70%, a massive increase over the analyst consensus of 45%, as tabulated by Bloomberg . And that huge increase, Kress noted, was despite a “supply constrained outlook.” In other words, if supply constraints ease, things could be even better. In response, the shares turned green after hours. Heading into Nvidia’s earnings, investors might not yet have been taking the AI boom for granted, but they are at least getting very used to it. Entrypoint cited Joseph Niles of Macro Risk Advisors pointing out that the implied move for Nvidia shares ahead of its earnings release was “the lowest in the AI era.” Investors had arguably been stuck on a bit of a hedonic treadmill , and a combination of muted performance heading into earnings and the Krees bombshell of operation optimism seems to have recalibrated Wall Street’s tastebuds. … and it’s not being complacent.
